association_basis: Phone filename timestamp around 09:09:23 local and video calibration/positioning/closing/pull sequence match the first 10 mm trial initialized at 09:09:25 local; the repeat was initialized at 09:12:38.
observations: Cube is on the table and the operator holds its other faces during final closing and pulling.
TPU pad shape changes during closing against the cube.
During the upward pull, the pads deform and move along the cube face while the cube appears to remain against the tabletop.
The gripper opens after the pull stop; the cube stays on the table.
interpretation: Video supports combined elastic pad deformation and relative sliding. It supports using the recorded 8.17 N opposing-load peak and subsequent weakening as effective gripper behavior, rather than calling the 33 N closed-baseline change a holding force.
limitations: Video and RTDE have no shared event synchronization; window boundaries are approximate.
Camera viewpoint and hidden contact patches prevent a reliable timestamp for the first microscopic slip.
Cube position and hand restraint were not instrumented; visible stationarity is qualitative.
The later 40 percent force-drop stop is not the start of sliding and does not establish a static breakaway peak.
